Challenge: Be An Earth System Trend Detective!

The learning problem

Environmental claims need inspectable evidence

Teachers and students need a clear path from a regional question to a source, a trend estimate and its uncertainty.

KILLA makes that path visible in an interface that keeps the evidence close to the explanation.

Example investigation

Has the sampled area warmed over the available record?

The learner examines the variable, the period and the assumptions behind the answer.

The official challenge asks teams to visualize Earth science time series and quantify the size and significance of trends.

NASA data

NASA POWER, with source context

25 annual observations per series, covering 2001–2025.

NASA POWER supplies MERRA-2 reanalysis estimates for sample cells near Esmeraldas and Cuenca. The meteorological grid is 0.5° latitude by 0.625° longitude.

T2M

Annual mean air temperature at 2 metresDegrees Celsius (°C)

PRECTOTCORR

Annual mean daily precipitationMillimetres per day (mm/day). These values are not annual totals.

The source and processing record belong with every result.

Source: NASA POWER API v2.10.0, MERRA2. Monthly and Annual API · Meteorological sources. Annual YYYY13 entries retain the reported NASA values.

An example from the record

Temperature trends in the selected cells

Ordinary least squares estimates for 2001–2025 annual mean 2-metre air temperature. All numbers are degrees Celsius per decade. Intervals are nominal 95 percent Student t intervals.
Sample cellChange per decadeNominal 95% interval
Near Esmeraldas0.96° N, 79.65° W+0.329 °C+0.119 to +0.539 °C
Near Cuenca2.90° S, 79.00° W+0.132 °C−0.118 to +0.382 °C

These exploratory estimates describe the selected 25-year window and sample grid cells. They do not represent averages over an entire city or province. The intervals assume independent residuals and omit model and representation uncertainty.

NASA POWER annual T2M entries, 2001–2025. OLS calculations and full-precision results appear in the project's downloadable data record. Open the live data view.

Method and limits

Trend estimates need uncertainty

y = a + bt

The fitted slope describes the estimated change per decade. The nominal 95% interval uses the Student t distribution with n − 2 degrees of freedom.

Ordinary least squares is an accessible starting point for investigating historical time series.

Exploratory interpretation

Climate records can contain correlated years. A basic OLS interval assumes independent residuals, so its coverage needs further checking.

Four location-variable comparisons remain exploratory, with no adjustment for multiple comparisons. The prototype omits p-values.

Causal attribution and local verification require further evidence.

Classroom use

An investigation students can explain

A teacher can turn one environmental question into a short exercise in reading evidence.

Learners compare locations and discuss how the selected variable, period and assumptions shape the answer.

Before inspecting the record

Write a claim and identify the observations needed to assess it.

After inspecting the record

Explain the trend, cite the source and name a limitation that affects the claim.

This is a proposed teaching activity. Classroom outcomes require evaluation.
